title: Testing the Rule in Genes and Time

scenes.visual: Title card: Testing the Rule in Genes and Time.

scenes.tts: A few genes have functional copies in humans, and not in chimpanzees. Do any of them change what progenitors do?
scenes.visual: A board with three columns: gene or change, tested in, effect on progenitors. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: A few genes have functional copies in humans, and not in chimpanzees. Do any of them change what progenitors do?

scenes.tts: No gene has been removed from a developing human brain. So each was tested in another system.
scenes.visual: Icons along the top of the board: mouse, ferret, marmoset, organoid, cultured slice.
scenes.narration: No gene has been removed from a developing human brain. So each was tested in another system.

scenes.tts: First, A R H G A P eleven B.
scenes.caption: First, ARHGAP11B.
scenes.visual: Gene card: ARHGAP11B, a partial copy of ARHGAP11A.

scenes.tts: In embryonic mouse cortex, it increased basal progenitors. In marmoset fetuses, it enlarged the neocortex.
scenes.visual: Board row: ARHGAP11B; mouse embryo, more basal progenitors; ferret; marmoset fetus, larger neocortex.
scenes.narration: In embryonic mouse cortex, it increased basal progenitors. In marmoset fetuses, it enlarged the neocortex.

scenes.tts: In cultured human fetal slices, blocking it reduced basal progenitors.
scenes.visual: Row extends: cultured human fetal slice, blocked, fewer basal progenitors.
scenes.narration: In cultured human fetal slices, blocking it reduced basal progenitors.

scenes.tts: Next, Notch two N L, which raises Notch signalling. In mouse cortex, it kept progenitors dividing and delayed neurons.
scenes.caption: Next, NOTCH2NL, which raises Notch signalling. In mouse cortex, it kept progenitors dividing and delayed neurons.
scenes.visual: Gene card: NOTCH2NL, derived from part of NOTCH2. Board row: mouse embryo, progenitors kept dividing.
scenes.narration: Next, NOTCH2NL, which raises Notch signalling. In mouse cortex, it kept progenitors dividing and delayed neurons.

scenes.tts: Deleted in human organoids, it made progenitors differentiate early.
scenes.visual: Row extends: human organoid, deleted, early differentiation.
scenes.narration: Deleted in human organoids, it made progenitors differentiate early.

scenes.tts: Both are consistent with more doubling. But the studies described here did not score division modes, so none shows which kind of division changed.
scenes.visual: Effect column filled: more basal progenitors; progenitors kept dividing, neurons delayed. Note under both rows: consistent with more doubling, divisions not scored.
scenes.narration: Both are consistent with more doubling. But the studies described here did not score division modes, so none shows which kind of division changed.

scenes.tts: Time matters too. Neurogenesis takes about a week in the mouse, roughly two months in the rhesus monkey, and longer in humans.
scenes.visual: Board row: neurogenesis timed. Bars: mouse about a week; rhesus roughly two months; human longer still.
scenes.narration: Time matters too. Neurogenesis takes about a week in the mouse, roughly two months in the rhesus monkey, and longer in humans.

scenes.tts: Extra time allows more rounds, if cell cycles do not lengthen. A steady pool adds in step with time. A growing pool compounds.
scenes.visual: Two lineage sketches over a longer bar: one growing in a single line, labelled steady pool, twice the time, twice the neurons; one widening, labelled growing pool, gain compounds.
scenes.narration: Extra time allows more rounds, if cell cycles do not lengthen. A steady pool adds in step with time. A growing pool compounds.

scenes.tts: One more difference lies outside the rule. Human neurons mature slowly. Spine density in prefrontal cortex stays above adult levels into the third decade.
scenes.visual: A separate box below the board: outside the rule, maturation. A dendrite with many spines; a timeline to the twenties.
scenes.narration: One more difference lies outside the rule. Human neurons mature slowly. Spine density in prefrontal cortex stays above adult levels into the third decade.

scenes.tts: S R G A P two C slowed spine maturation in mouse neurons.
scenes.caption: SRGAP2C slowed spine maturation in mouse neurons.
scenes.visual: Gene card in the maturation box: SRGAP2C, mouse cortical neurons, slower spine maturation.
scenes.narration: SRGAP2C slowed spine maturation in mouse neurons.

scenes.tts: Is that pace set by the body, or the cells? Predict. Human neurons go into newborn mouse cortex. Whose pace do they keep?
scenes.visual: A human neuron placed among mouse neurons in a newborn mouse cortex. Question card.
scenes.narration: Is that pace set by the body, or the cells? Predict. Human neurons go into newborn mouse cortex. Whose pace do they keep?

scenes.visual: Question card held.

scenes.tts: They matured over many months, close to a human time course. The mouse neurons around them had long since matured.
scenes.visual: Timeline: mouse neurons mature in weeks; the human neuron matures over many months.
scenes.narration: They matured over many months, close to a human time course. The mouse neurons around them had long since matured.

scenes.tts: At least part of the timing travels with the cells.
scenes.visual: Caption: timing travels with the cells.
scenes.narration: At least part of the timing travels with the cells.

scenes.visual: The transplant held.

scenes.tts: But maturation shapes connections, not neuron number. It lies outside the rule.
scenes.visual: The maturation box stays separate from the doubling board.
scenes.narration: But maturation shapes connections, not neuron number. It lies outside the rule.

scenes.tts: And no test shows that one gene made the human cortex.
scenes.visual: Caption across the board: none shows that one gene made the human cortex.
scenes.narration: And no test shows that one gene made the human cortex.

scenes.tts: Multiply, don't add: a leading explanation for our large cortex. How much came from founders, outer radial glia, or a longer clock is still open.
scenes.visual: Closing card: Multiply, don't add. A leading explanation. Open: founders, outer radial glia, or a longer clock?
scenes.narration: Multiply, don't add: a leading explanation for our large cortex. How much came from founders, outer radial glia, or a longer clock is still open.

scenes.visual: Closing card held.
